bangkok.t: The capital where old temples, high-rises, and street food share the same soi

chiang-mai.t: An old town in the valley that’s easy to stay in longer than planned

phuket.t: A big Andaman island with white-sand beaches, a Sino-Portuguese old town, and Hokkien food

krabi.t: Andaman limestone cliffs, white-sand beaches, clear islands, rock climbing at Railay, and emerald-green water

chiang-rai.t: Thailand’s northernmost city, with striking temples, high mountains, and tea farms

chonburi.t: Thailand’s eastern seaboard — Pattaya, nearby islands, and fresh seafood, all a short drive from Bangkok

surat-thani.t: The ’town of a hundred islands’ on the Gulf of Thailand — gateway to Samui, Cheow Lan Lake, and the old temple town of Chaiya

prachuap-khiri-khan.t: Thailand’s narrowest province, home to Hua Hin, the three-bay coast of Prachuap, Khao Takiab, and Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park

kanchanaburi.t: Home of the Bridge over the River Kwai, big waterfalls, the forested west, and riverside raft houses you can stay on all year

ayutthaya.t: A former royal capital and World Heritage city — wander old temple ruins and cycle the island.

rayong.t: An eastern seaside province with Koh Samet, quiet beaches, fruit orchards, and famous dried seafood

trat.t: Thailand’s last province on the eastern coast, home to Koh Chang, Koh Kood, and Koh Mak — clear water and quiet seas

phang-nga.t: Limestone-bay country on the Andaman — home to James Bond Island, the Similans, and Khao Lak

nan.t: An old town in a valley with pretty temples, good coffee, and mountain roads up to the morning mist

mae-hong-son.t: City of three mists at the end of the winding road

sukhothai.t: A World Heritage city — old stupas scattered across open fields

nakhon-ratchasima.t: The gateway to Isan — Khao Yai, Khmer temples, and vineyards an easy drive from Bangkok

phetchabun.t: Mist over Khao Kho, chilly nights on Phu Tab Berk, and the sweet tamarind the province is known for

lamphun.t: A quiet little town that’s the oldest in the North

lampang.t: Horse carriages and old temples — a town made for slow walks all day

phayao.t: A small town by the lake where you slow down and watch the sunset every evening

phrae.t: Teak houses and indigo-dyed cloth, an old town to wander slowly

uttaradit.t: Home of langsat fruit, Sirikit Dam, and the legendary town of Laplae

phitsanulok.t: Home of the Phra Phuttha Chinnarat, gateway to the eastern mountains

tak.t: A western border province with a huge waterfall deep in the jungle

kamphaeng-phet.t: A quiet World Heritage town known for its sweet egg bananas

phichit.t: Chalawan’s town, Bueng Si Fai, and riverside life along the Nan

nakhon-sawan.t: Pak Nam Pho, where the Chao Phraya River begins and the biggest Chinese New Year in Thailand happens

uthai-thani.t: A small town on the Sakae Krang River, next to the Huai Kha Khaeng World Heritage forest

buriram.t: Stone temples on extinct volcanoes, plus the home of Thai football and big-league motorsport

surin.t: Elephant country, Khmer temples, and the handwoven silk of southern Isan

sisaket.t: Volcanic-soil durian, Khmer temples, and the Khao Phra Wihan border trail in the deep south of Isan

ubon-ratchathani.t: A Mekong-side city in Thailand’s far east — Pha Taem, Sam Phan Bok, and the Candle Festival

yasothon.t: Home of the rocket festival, Phra That Kong Khao Noi, and the Ban Singha Tha old town

chaiyaphum.t: Pink siam tulip fields in the rains, the stone pillars of Mo Hin Khao, and Ban Khwao silk

amnat-charoen.t: A small town in the southern Isan, home to the giant Phra Mongkhon Ming Muang Buddha and quiet rice-field life

nong-bua-lamphu.t: A small town below the Phu Phan range, Luang Pu Khao’s Wat Tham Klong Phen, and the Ubolratana reservoir

khon-kaen.t: Isaan’s hub city — dinosaurs, Bueng Kaen Nakhon lake, and countryside mudmee silk

udon-thani.t: The big city of the upper Isan, with the Ban Chiang World Heritage site, the Red Lotus Sea, and great Vietnamese food

loei.t: Cool mountain air, the Phu Kradueng sea of fog, and the Phi Ta Khon festival in Dan Sai

nong-khai.t: A Mekong border town with the Friendship Bridge to Laos, Sala Kaew Ku, and the Naga fireballs

maha-sarakham.t: The education hub of central Isan — Phra That Na Dun, ancient Khmer ruins, and a lively student scene

roi-et.t: Home of Bueng Phlan Chai, the great Phra Maha Chedi Chai Mongkol, and the Thung Kula Ronghai plains

kalasin.t: Isan’s dinosaur town — Praewa silk, Lam Pao Dam, and the Phu Phan range

sakon-nakhon.t: Home of Wat Phra That Choeng Chum, hand-dyed indigo cloth, the wide Nong Han lake, and the Phu Phan hills

nakhon-phanom.t: A Mekong town facing the mountains of Laos — Phra That Phanom, an evening riverside walk, and an old Vietnamese quarter

mukdahan.t: A Mekong border town across from Savannakhet — the Indochina Market, Ho Kaeo Mukdahan tower, and the rock views of Phu Pha Thoep

bueng-kan.t: Isan’s newest Mekong town — Phu Tok’s wooden stairways, the Three Whale Rocks, and rubber plantations as far as you can see

nonthaburi.t: A Chao Phraya riverside town that blends seamlessly into Bangkok

pathum-thani.t: Rangsit at the end of the train line, canal-side rice fields, theme parks, and a big science museum

samut-prakan.t: The river-mouth town on the Gulf of Thailand, with old forts, the Ancient City, and seaside fish markets

samut-sakhon.t: Mahachai, the port town on the Gulf with a huge fish market, salt flats, and fresh seafood

samut-songkhram.t: The small riverside town of Mae Klong, where three waters meet — home to the Maeklong Railway Market, Amphawa Floating Market, and coconut groves everywhere

nakhon-pathom.t: Home of the giant Phra Pathom Chedi, next door to Bangkok, with old markets, floating markets, and loads of famous food

ang-thong.t: A flat river plain with a giant Buddha, old temples, craft villages, and life along the Chao Phraya

lopburi.t: City of monkeys and King Narai’s palace, with sunflower fields in the cool season

sing-buri.t: Home of the Bang Rachan heroes, Mae La snakehead fish, and old temples along the Chao Phraya River

chai-nat.t: A Chao Phraya riverside town with a bird park, a big dam, and the old town of Sankhaburi

saraburi.t: Home of the Buddha’s Footprint, Muak Lek milk, and waterfalls at the foot of Khao Yai

suphan-buri.t: An old town on the Tha Chin River — home of luk thung music, century-old markets, and a city where everything worth seeing sits close together

nakhon-nayok.t: Waterfall country at the foot of Khao Yai near Bangkok, with rafting, camping, and local fruit

chanthaburi.t: An eastern town of fruit and gemstones, with an old riverside community, mountains, and the sea

chachoengsao.t: Home of Luang Pho Sothon on the Bang Pakong River, an easy trip from Bangkok with old markets, big temples, and mango orchards

prachinburi.t: Home of Abhaibhubejhr herbal medicine, the eastern foothills of Khao Yai, with ancient ruins, the Hin Phoeng rapids, and sweet santol fruit

sa-kaeo.t: An eastern border province next to Cambodia, with Rong Kluea Market, Khmer temples, hills, and waterfalls

ratchaburi.t: The dragon-jar town on the Mae Klong River, home to Damnoen Saduak floating market, Khao Ngu caves, and the Tenasserim hills out at Suan Phueng

phetchaburi.t: An old town on the Phetchaburi River with the Phra Nakhon Khiri palace, craftsman temples, mor kaeng custard, and the beaches of Cha-am and Laem Phak Bia

chumphon.t: The gateway to the south, with long Sai Ri Beach, the Prince of Chumphon’s warship, dive islands, and robusta coffee

ranong.t: An Andaman coast town of hot springs, Koh Phayam, and the Myanmar border, known for eight months of rain and four of sun

nakhon-si-thammarat.t: A thousand-year-old stupa, Ai Khai of Wat Chedi, shadow-puppet cafes, and waterfalls plus the Gulf coast

phatthalung.t: A lakeside town on Songkhla Lake — Khao Ok Thalu mountain, red lotus blooms at Thale Noi, rice fields with water buffalo, and the home of shadow puppetry and Manora dance

trang.t: The Andaman coast’s food town — morning roast pork, hot dim sum, the Emerald Cave, and quiet islands made for slow nights

satun.t: A southern border town on the Andaman, a UNESCO Global Geopark, the Tarutao–Koh Lipe islands, and a quiet Muslim way of life

songkhla.t: A two-sea province with a colorful old town, Samila Beach and its mermaid, the Nang Ngam street quarter, and the border trade city of Hat Yai

pattani.t: An old southern port town with a Malay soul — historic mosques, a Sino-Portuguese old quarter, and bold local food

yala.t: Thailand’s southernmost province — a town laid out in perfect circles, plus Betong with the Aiyoeweng sea of fog, an old tunnel, and Hokkien Chinese food

narathiwat.t: Thailand’s southernmost province on the Gulf coast — a Malay-flavored border town with long sandy beaches, the Toh Daeng peat swamp, and bold local food
